requirement_text: The duties of the AI Center of Excellence shall include convening relevant stakeholders, publishing information on AI programs and initiatives, advising GSA, OMB, agencies, and OSTP, assisting agencies in applying Federal policies, and consulting with agencies that operate or support AI-related programs.
evidence_title: Artificial intelligence | GSA
audit_reason: The GSA AI hub provides direct evidence of several ongoing AI Center of Excellence functions, but not enough to verify every statutory duty in full.

requirement_text: OMB, coordinating with OSTP, GSA, and other relevant agencies and stakeholders, shall issue draft and final memorandum guidance on Federal acquisition and use of AI, barriers to agency AI use, discriminatory impact and bias mitigation, and the template for agency compliance plans, and shall update that memorandum every two years for ten years.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: The public OMB memoranda are direct evidence that the high-level guidance deliverables were eventually issued.

requirement_text: Heads of agencies shall submit to OMB and post publicly either a plan to achieve consistency with the OMB memorandum or a written determination that the agency does not use and does not anticipate using AI.
evidence_title: AI strategies and compliance plan | GSA
audit_reason: Public agency compliance-plan pages support a cautious Partially implemented coding because the audit did not verify every agency's posting or determination.

requirement_text: The OPM Director shall identify AI-related skills and competencies, establish or update an AI occupational series, estimate the number of Federal employees in AI-related positions by agency, and prepare two-year and five-year workforce forecasts.
evidence_title: The Artificial Intelligence Classification Policy and Talent Acquisition Guidance - The AI in Government Act of 2020
audit_reason: OPM's published guidance is direct public evidence for the workforce-skills and classification work described in this row.

requirement_text: The OPM Director shall submit to the relevant congressional committees a comprehensive plan with a timeline to complete the requirements described in section 105(a).
evidence_title: The Artificial Intelligence Classification Policy and Talent Acquisition Guidance - The AI in Government Act of 2020
audit_reason: The audit still did not locate a public copy of the specific plan to Congress required by section 105(b), so keeping Unable to verify is the conservative choice.

requirement_text: Implementing agencies shall pursue six strategic objectives to promote and protect American advances in AI, including sustained AI R&D, access to Federal data and computing resources, reduced barriers to AI use, technical standards, and AI workforce development.
evidence_title: AI.Gov | President Trump's AI Strategy and Action Plan
audit_reason: The cited AI.Gov page is broad, strategic context rather than direct public evidence that agencies pursued the full set of objectives in this requirement.

requirement_text: Heads of AI R&D agencies shall explore opportunities for collaboration with non-Federal entities, including the private sector, academia, nonprofits, subnational governments, and foreign partners and allies.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The row is already coded conservatively because the public evidence is broad and not requirement-specific.

requirement_text: Heads of all agencies shall review Federal data and models to identify opportunities to increase access and use by the non-Federal AI research community, including improvements to inventory documentation and the prioritization of quality and access improvements.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The requirement is already held at Unable to verify because the available public evidence does not prove agency-by-agency review activity.

requirement_text: OMB, with interagency councils and the NSTC Select Committee on AI, shall update implementation guidance for Enterprise Data Inventories and Source Code Inventories to support discovery and usability in AI R&D.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The public guidance portal does not directly establish that the required inventory-guidance update was completed, so keeping Unable to verify is the safer choice.

requirement_text: Agencies shall consider methods to improve the quality, usability, and appropriate access to priority data by the AI research community and identify associated resource implications.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The evidence remains too general to verify agency consideration of data quality and access improvements across government.

requirement_text: Agencies, coordinating with privacy officials, statistical entities, data managers, and other relevant personnel, shall identify barriers or requirements associated with increased access to and use of data and models, including privacy, safety, security, documentation, governance, and related considerations.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The available public materials do not document completion of the specific barrier-identification exercise described in the requirement.

requirement_text: Agencies shall identify opportunities to use new technologies and best practices to increase access to and usability of open data and models, while exploring appropriate controls on access to sensitive or restricted data and models.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The public record supports related open-data work but not the specific agency identification of new technologies and controls required here.

requirement_text: The Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Health and Human Services, and Energy, the NASA Administrator, and the NSF Director shall prioritize the allocation of high-performance computing resources for AI-related applications through discretionary reserves or other mechanisms.
evidence_title: Artificial Intelligence Research and Development - NITRD Program
audit_reason: The cited NITRD evidence shows federal coordination, but it does not directly verify that the named agencies prioritized high-performance computing allocations for AI applications.

requirement_text: The NSTC Select Committee on AI shall provide technical expertise to the American Technology Council on AI and the modernization of Federal technology, data, and digital service delivery.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The public evidence is still too general to verify that agencies created or maintained the specific access pathways implied by this provision.

requirement_text: Implementing agencies that also have regulatory authorities shall review their authorities and submit plans to OMB to achieve consistency with the OMB memorandum issued under section 6(a).
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: Later AI-use memoranda do not clearly replace the original M-21-06-specific plan submission obligation for agencies with regulatory authorities.

requirement_text: Implementing agencies that provide educational grants shall consider AI as a priority area within existing Federal fellowship and service programs and shall annually communicate plans for doing so to the NSTC Select Committee on AI.
evidence_title: AI.Gov | President Trump's AI Strategy and Action Plan
audit_reason: Public AI education activity exists, but the evidence does not directly verify the required annual agency communications to the NSTC Select Committee.

requirement_text: The NSTC Select Committee on AI shall provide recommendations to the NSTC Committee on STEM Education regarding AI-related educational and workforce development considerations that focus on American citizens.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: The evidence remains too general to verify agency identification of AI-related workforce needs under this specific requirement.

requirement_text: The NSTC Select Committee on AI shall provide technical expertise to the National Council for the American Worker on AI and the American workforce.
evidence_title: resources.data.gov
audit_reason: No direct public evidence was found for the specific policy development obligation in this row, so keeping Unable to verify is appropriate.

requirement_text: The Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, coordinating with OSTP and relevant agencies, shall organize and submit to the President an action plan to protect the United States advantage in AI and related critical technologies against strategic competitors and adversarial nations.
evidence_title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Signs Historic Directive on AI in the National Security Enterprise
audit_reason: A White House fact sheet shows a newer national-security AI directive, but it does not directly establish that this earlier action-plan requirement was formally replaced or completed.

requirement_text: Agencies that are recipients of the action plan described in section 8(a)-(b) shall implement that action plan.
evidence_title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Signs Historic Directive on AI in the National Security Enterprise
audit_reason: The public record does not clearly show whether agencies implemented the original action plan or whether that obligation was formally replaced by the newer directive.

requirement_text: Responsible agencies shall, when considering the design, development, acquisition, and use of AI in Government, be guided by the order's principles in order to foster public trust and remain consistent with law.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: M-25-21 directly reaffirms governance and public-trust expectations tied to EO 13960, which is enough for a cautious Partially implemented judgment but not a full upgrade.

requirement_text: To the extent existing OMB policies that address information and information technology design, development, acquisition, and use are consistent with the order's principles and applicable law, those policies shall continue to apply.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: The current OMB governance memorandum is direct evidence that relevant AI policies continue to operate, but not enough to prove full requirement-level completion across government.

requirement_text: OMB shall publicly post a roadmap for policy guidance that it intends to create or revise to better support the use of AI in Government, including a schedule for public engagement and finalization where appropriate.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: Later OMB AI memoranda exist, but the audit did not locate direct public evidence that the specific roadmap deliverable was posted or formally superseded.

requirement_text: Agencies shall continue to use voluntary consensus standards developed with industry participation where available and appropriate, and OMB shall take such standards into account when revising or developing AI guidance.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: The row is already conservatively coded because the cited evidence does not directly verify use of voluntary consensus standards in the specific sense required here.

requirement_text: The CIO Council, coordinating with relevant interagency bodies, shall identify, provide guidance on, and make publicly available the criteria, format, and mechanisms for agency inventories of non-classified and non-sensitive AI use cases.
evidence_title: AI Use Case Inventory | US EPA
audit_reason: Agency inventory pages suggest common practice, but the audit did not find direct public evidence of the CIO Council guidance artifact required by the row.

requirement_text: Responsible agencies shall prepare an inventory of non-classified and non-sensitive AI use cases, including current and planned uses, and update that inventory annually.
evidence_title: Department of Justice | AI Inventory
audit_reason: Multiple agency public inventory pages support a cautious Partially implemented judgment, even though the audit did not verify every covered agency individually.

requirement_text: As part of their inventories, agencies shall identify, review, and assess existing AI deployed and operating in support of agency missions for any inconsistencies with the order.
evidence_title: Department of Justice | AI Inventory
audit_reason: Public inventory methodology is indirect, but it still supports a limited conclusion that some review-and-assessment activity is occurring.

requirement_text: Agencies shall develop plans either to achieve consistency with the order for each AI application or to retire applications found not to be consistent with the order, and those plans must be approved by the responsible officials.
evidence_title: Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-24-10
audit_reason: The available public evidence does not directly verify completion of agency planning obligations tied to this row, so keeping Unable to verify is appropriate.

requirement_text: Agencies shall strive to implement the approved plans for AI applications, subject to existing resource levels and in coordination with the Agency Data Governance Body and relevant officials.
evidence_title: Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-24-10
audit_reason: This row was originally excluded from the paper's aggregate count, and the current public evidence still does not verify completion of the implementation step itself.

requirement_text: Agencies shall share their AI inventories with other agencies, to the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law and policy, through coordination by the CIO and Chief Data Officer Councils.
evidence_title: Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-24-10
audit_reason: The public record does not clearly verify the cross-agency sharing obligation, so the conservative Unable to verify coding should stand.

requirement_text: Agencies shall make their AI inventories available to the public, to the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law and policy.
evidence_title: Department of Justice | AI Inventory
audit_reason: Public agency inventory pages are direct evidence that some agencies are posting inventories, but the audit did not confirm universal coverage, so Partially implemented remains appropriate.

requirement_text: The CIO Council shall publish a list of recommended interagency bodies and forums in which agencies may elect to participate to advance the AI principles.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: The newer governance structure does not directly verify that the required CIO Council list was published or formally replaced by a clearly equivalent deliverable.

requirement_text: Agencies are expected to participate in interagency bodies for the purpose of advancing implementation of the principles and the use of AI consistent with the order.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: M-25-21 directly establishes an interagency Chief AI Officer Council, which supports a cautious partial-implementation judgment for participation requirements.

requirement_text: OPM, coordinating with GSA and other relevant agencies, shall create an inventory of Federal Government rotational programs and determine how they can be used to expand the number of employees with AI expertise.
evidence_title: Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-24-10
audit_reason: The current public materials do not directly document the specific rotational-program inventory required here, so retaining Unable to verify is the safer choice.

requirement_text: OPM shall issue a report with recommendations on how rotational programs can best be used to expand the number of employees with AI expertise at agencies.
evidence_title: Department of Justice Compliance Plan for OMB Memorandum M-24-10
audit_reason: No direct public copy of the required OPM recommendations report was identified in the audit, so the row should remain Unable to verify.

requirement_text: Agencies shall specify the responsible official or officials who will coordinate implementation of the order's principles with the agency data governance body and relevant officials and collaborate with the interagency bodies.
evidence_title: OMB Memorandum M-25-21: Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust
audit_reason: M-25-21 directly requires agencies to designate Chief AI Officers and governance structures, which clearly absorbs the older responsible-official coordination role.
